sections.label: Budget deficit and COVID spending
sections.summary: The Government committed nearly $100 billion through five Budgets, with a FY2020 deficit of $64.9 billion, or 13.9% of GDP.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Last year, in addition to our usual spending, the Government committed nearly $100 billion through five Budgets to support Singaporeans, help tide businesses over this difficult period, and most importantly, keep everyone safe.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The overall Budget deficit for Financial Year 2020 is also the largest since Singapore’s independence, at $64.9 billion, or 13.9% of GDP.

sections.label: Effects of fiscal measures
sections.summary: Without these measures, GDP would have shrunk at least 12.4%, and they are estimated to save or create 155,000 jobs.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Without the fiscal and monetary policy measures, Singapore’s GDP would have shrunk by at least 12.4%, more than double the contraction we experienced.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: These measures are also estimated to save or create 155,000 jobs on average over 2020 and 2021, preventing the resident unemployment rate from rising a further two percentage points in 2020.

sections.label: Growth projection and Resilience Package
sections.summary: The economy is projected to grow 4% to 6%, and $11 billion is set aside for a COVID-19 Resilience Package.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The Singapore economy is projected to grow between 4% and 6%, with some sectors growing well, and others remaining under stress.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: I will set aside $11 billion for a COVID-19 Resilience Package.

sections.label: COVID-19 vaccination numbers
sections.summary: As of 14 February, close to 250,000 people received a first dose, and about 55,000 also received a second dose.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: As of 14 February this year, close to 250,000 people have received their first dose of the COVID-19 vaccine, of which about 55,000 have also received their second dose.

sections.label: Public health funding
sections.summary: $4.8 billion of the COVID-19 Resilience Package is dedicated to public health and safe re-opening measures.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Altogether, I will be dedicating $4.8 billion of the COVID-19 Resilience Package towards public health and safe re-opening measures.

sections.label: Jobs Support Scheme support
sections.summary: Support was tapered for recovering sectors and extended to harder-hit ones, with over $25 billion committed to the JSS.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: As the situation improved, I tapered support for sectors that were recovering well, and extended support to harder-hit sectors.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: So far, we have committed over $25 billion to the JSS, and supported over 150,000 employers for up to 17 months.

sections.label: JSS extension for Tier 1 sectors
sections.summary: JSS is extended by six months for firms in aviation, aerospace and tourism.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: For firms in Tier 1 sectors – aviation, aerospace and tourism, I will extend JSS by six months.

sections.label: Cost of JSS extension
sections.summary: The JSS extension will cost $700 million overall.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Overall, the JSS extension will cost $700 million.

sections.label: Funding for packages extension
sections.summary: $45 million is set aside for extension and enhancements to these packages.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We look forward to activities resuming, with greater vibrancy.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: I will set aside $45 million for the extension and enhancements to these packages.

sections.label: COVAX and global vaccine access
sections.summary: Singapore works with like-minded countries through COVAX to promote global vaccine access and safe travel resumption.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The global economy will remain stunted for as long as there are countries that have yet to suppress COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: This is why Singapore is working with like-minded countries through the COVAX facility, to promote global access to the vaccine and help accelerate the resumption of safe travels.

sections.label: Allocation for firms and workers
sections.summary: $24 billion is allocated over three years to help firms and workers emerge stronger.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Over the next three years, I will allocate $24 billion to enable our firms and workers to emerge stronger.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The efforts will span several years, but it is crucial that we start today.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: This builds on the momentum of the transformation push started five years ago, when we launched our Industry Transformation Maps.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: In this financial year, I will focus on how we can move decisively to build three enablers for this next phase of transformation, to emerge stronger.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: First, to grow a vibrant business community, with a strong spirit of innovation and enterprise, deeply connected with Asia and the world.

sections.label: Restoring Changi connectivity and biosafety
sections.summary: Changi's connectivity will be restored and on-arrival testing and biosafety systems invested in.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: To secure our position as a key aviation hub and maintain Changi’s position as a safe, trusted and well-connected airport for travellers and employees alike, we will restore Changi’s connectivity and invest in on-arrival testing and biosafety systems.

sections.label: Corporate Venture Launchpad pilot
sections.summary: The Corporate Venture Launchpad will be piloted this year to drive new innovative ventures, providing co-funding for corporates to build ventures through pre-qualified venture studios.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The first platform is the Corporate Venture Launchpad, which will be piloted this year to drive new innovative ventures.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The Launchpad will provide co-funding for corporates to build new ventures through pre-qualified venture studios.

sections.label: Overseas innovation launchpad participation
sections.summary: Since 2017, over 650 students and about 780 Singapore businesses have taken part in overseas innovation launchpads, 40% in Southeast Asia.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Since its inception in 2017, over 650 students and about 780 Singapore businesses have taken part in innovation launchpads overseas. 40% of these were in Southeast Asia.

sections.label: GIA network expansion
sections.summary: The GIA network has 15 city links, will expand to more than 25 cities over five years, and supports up to 70% of qualifying costs.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The GIA network currently has 15 city links, including four Southeast Asian cities – Bangkok, Ho Chi Minh City, Jakarta and Manila.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: I will expand it to more than 25 cities around the globe over the next five years.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The Programme will support up to 70% of qualifying costs for cross-border innovation and partnership projects.

sections.label: ASEAN GDP and trade
sections.summary: ASEAN nations had a collective GDP of US$3.2 trillion in 2019, the world's fifth largest economy, and became China's largest trading partner in 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The ASEAN nations had a GDP of US$3.2 trillion collectively in 2019, making it the world’s fifth largest economy.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The ASEAN region also became China’s largest trading partner in 2020.

sections.label: SBF overseas offices
sections.summary: The Singapore Business Federation will officially open two new overseas offices soon, one in Jakarta and one in Ho Chi Minh City.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: To add on to these efforts, the Singapore Business Federation will be officially opening two new overseas offices soon – one in Jakarta and one in Ho Chi Minh City.

sections.label: Venture Debt programme support
sections.summary: The Government shares up to 70% of risk on eligible loans, will raise the loan quantum cap from $5 million to $8 million, expecting about $45 million catalysed.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: As part of the Venture Debt programme, the Government shares up to 70% of the risk on eligible loans with Participating Financial Institutions.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: I will continue to support this programme, and increase the cap on loan quantum supported, from $5 million to $8 million.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: With this, we expect about $45 million of venture debt to be catalysed over the next year.

sections.label: One billion for schemes
sections.summary: The speaker is setting aside $1 billion for these schemes, including the enhancements.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Including these enhancements, I am setting aside $1 billion for these schemes.

sections.label: Job Redesign grant co-funding
sections.summary: The Productivity Solutions Grant – Job Redesign co-funding ratio rises from 70% to 80% until end-March 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: To support businesses in redesigning jobs, I will enhance the Productivity Solutions Grant – Job Redesign, by raising the Government’s co-funding ratio from 70% to 80%, till end-March 2022.

sections.label: Local Enterprises Funding Platform
sections.summary: $500 million is set aside to be co-invested with Temasek in a commercially managed Local Enterprises Funding Platform, matched one-for-one.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: To ensure growth capital is available for LLEs that are ready to transform or expand overseas on a larger scale, I will complement existing grants and loans, and support them through equity investments, tapping on market players to ensure commercial discipline.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: I will set aside $500 million to be co-invested with Temasek in a Local Enterprises Funding Platform, to be managed commercially.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Temasek will match the Government’s funds on a one-for-one basis, so the platform will have $1 billion available for its investments.

sections.label: Growth and Transformation Scheme launch
sections.summary: Building on Alliances for Action, the speaker will start with the Built Environment sector and launch the Growth and Transformation Scheme.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We will build on the Alliances for Action and begin with a few alliances first.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We will start with the Built Environment sector, where I will launch the Growth and Transformation Scheme or GTS.

sections.label: DfMA adoption doubled
sections.summary: Adoption for DfMA technologies doubled from 19% in 2017 to 39% in 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Adoption for DfMA technologies has doubled from 19% in 2017 to 39% in 2020.

sections.label: Mercer survey on remote productivity
sections.summary: A Mercer survey last year showed over 90% of employers globally saw similar or higher productivity despite remote work.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: A Mercer survey last year showed that over 90% of employers globally saw similar or higher productivity despite employees working remotely.

sections.label: Jobs and training placements
sections.summary: Nearly 76,000 individuals were placed into jobs, traineeships, attachments and skills training, and an estimated 110,000 local jobseekers were hired under the Jobs Growth Incentive.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: As of end last year, we have placed nearly 76,000 individuals into jobs, traineeships, attachments and skills training.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Under the Jobs Growth Incentive, or JGI, an estimated 110,000 local jobseekers were collectively hired within two months from the implementation of the scheme.

sections.label: Second tranche Jobs and Skills Package
sections.summary: An additional $5.4 billion is allocated to a second tranche of the Jobs and Skills Package, with $5.2 billion for JGI to extend the hiring window to end-September 2021.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: To enable our people to take on these new jobs, I will allocate an additional $5.4 billion to a second tranche of the Jobs and Skills Package, on top of the $3 billion allocated last year.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Of this, $5.2 billion will be allocated to JGI, to extend the hiring window by seven months, up to end-September 2021.

sections.label: SGUnited Jobs and Skills Package targets
sections.summary: Budget is set aside to support hiring of 200,000 locals this year through JGI and up to 35,000 traineeship and training opportunities.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Through the next phase of the SGUnited Jobs and Skills Package, we have set aside the budget to support the hiring of 200,000 locals this year through the JGI, and provide up to 35,000 traineeship and training opportunities to continue to support jobseekers in upskilling and accessing employment opportunities.

sections.label: Healthcare worker salaries
sections.summary: Salaries of nurses and other healthcare workers such as support care staff will be enhanced.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: This sector provides many good skilled jobs that are noble, meaningful and make a difference to Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We will enhance the salaries of our nurses and other healthcare workers such as support care staff.

sections.label: Wage Credit Scheme extension
sections.summary: The Wage Credit Scheme is extended for a year at a 15% co-funding level to support wage increments for companies to retain or draw in locals.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: In line with this, I will support the employment of Singaporeans while we deepen their capabilities and promote capability transfer, while moderating our reliance on foreign labour where we must.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: I will provide further help to support wage increments for companies to retain or draw in locals by extending the Wage Credit Scheme for a year, at a co-funding level of 15%.

sections.label: CTP extension
sections.summary: More than 140 companies and over 970 locals have benefitted or are expected to benefit from 40 projects, and the CTP will be extended to end-September 2024.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: As of end-2020, more than 140 companies, and over 970 locals have benefitted or are expected to benefit from 40 projects.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: I will extend the CTP up to end-September 2024.

sections.label: Reducing Manufacturing sub-DRC
sections.summary: The sub-DRC for Manufacturing will be reduced to 18% from 1 January 2022 and to 15% from 1 January 2023.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: But we should moderate further our reliance on them, so as to focus on creating good jobs for locals.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Therefore, we will reduce the sub-DRC for Manufacturing in two steps, to 18% from 1 January 2022, and to 15% from 1 January 2023.

sections.label: AfAs formed and announced
sections.summary: 15 AfAs have been formed or announced within eight months, and NCSS and SG Enable will form one on care-giver support.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Within eight months, 15 AfAs have been formed or announced, alongside other existing partnerships and collaborations.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Going forward, the National Council of Social Service and SG Enable will also form an AfA on support for care-givers of persons with disabilities.

sections.label: Household Support Package
sections.summary: A Household Support Package provides an extra $200 GST Voucher Cash Special Payment, additional U-Save rebates, and a $200 per child top-up.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: As the economic situation remains uncertain, I will introduce a Household Support Package, to provide additional support to families.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: All Singaporeans who are eligible for GST Voucher – Cash will receive an additional one-off GST Voucher – Cash Special Payment of $200.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: This is on top of the regular GST Voucher – Cash payment.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: I will also provide a GST Voucher – U-Save Special Payment to eligible HDB households, amounting to an additional 50% U-Save rebate over one year.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Each household will receive additional utilities rebates of between $120 and $200 this year.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Third, for families with Singaporean children below the age of 21, I will provide an additional top-up of $200 per child through the Child Development Account, Edusave Account, or Post-Secondary Education Account, to further support parents as they invest in their children’s future.

sections.label: CDC Vouchers for households
sections.summary: With the CDCs, all Singaporean households will receive $100 worth of CDC Vouchers for heartland shops and hawker centres.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: To thank all Singaporeans for their sense of solidarity, and to continue to support our heartland businesses and hawkers, I will partner the Community Development Councils, or CDCs, to give all Singaporean households $100 worth of CDC Vouchers per household, to be used at participating heartland shops and hawker centres.

sections.label: Expanding ComLink nationwide
sections.summary: MSF will receive resources to expand ComLink to a nationwide programme covering 14,000 families with children over two years.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: To provide holistic support to more families, I will provide resources for MSF to expand ComLink significantly – to a nationwide programme to eventually cover 14,000 families with children, over the next two years.

sections.label: Extending charity tax deductions
sections.summary: The 250% tax deduction for donations to IPCs is extended to end-2023, and Tote Board's Enhanced Fund-Raising Programme support is extended one year.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: To encourage Singaporeans to give back to the community and to provide strong support for the charity sector in this time of crisis, I will extend the 250% tax deduction for donations to IPCs for another two years, until the end of 2023.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: I will also extend the additional Government support for Tote Board’s Enhanced Fund-Raising Programme by one year.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Charities can apply to receive dollar-for-dollar matching on eligible donations, which are raised from projects in FY2021, up to a cap of $250,000 per applicant.

sections.label: ComChest giving support
sections.summary: Extends ComChest's SHARE as One matching period to FY2023 and sets aside $20 million for a new Change for Charity Grant.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: To encourage more giving during these challenging times, I will support ComChest in two areas: First, I will extend ComChest’s SHARE as One matching period to FY2023.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Second, I will set aside $20 million for a new Change for Charity Grant.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The Grant will match ComChest donations raised through this new initiative.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The grant also co-funds one-off development costs needed to integrate or enhance donation functions onto businesses’ payment platforms.

sections.label: Corporate volunteerism scheme extension
sections.summary: Extends the Business and IPC Partnership Scheme for another two years, until the end of 2023.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: To encourage more corporate volunteerism, I will extend the Business and IPC Partnership Scheme for another two years, until the end of 2023.

sections.label: CDC Care and Innovation Fund
sections.summary: Government will provide three dollars for every dollar raised for the CDCs' Care and Innovation Fund, setting aside $50m.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: To provide greater support for bottom-up, innovative initiatives which address the needs of the community, the Government will provide three dollars for every dollar raised, for the CDCs’ Care and Innovation Fund.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: I will set aside $50m for this matching grant.

sections.label: Singapore Green Plan 2030 launch
sections.summary: The Singapore Green Plan 2030 was launched last week.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Last week, we launched the Singapore Green Plan 2030.

sections.label: Agri-food technology adoption fund
sections.summary: Sets aside $60 million for a new Agri-Food Cluster Transformation Fund to support technology adoption in the agri-food sector.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: To continue supporting technology adoption in the agri-food sector, I will set aside $60 million for a new Agri-Food Cluster Transformation Fund.

sections.label: EV charging and adoption measures
sections.summary: Aims to deploy 60,000 charging points by 2030, sets aside $30 million for EV initiatives, and lowers the Additional Registration Fee floor to zero for electric cars.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We will accelerate the development of our charging infrastructure to better support the growth of EVs in the next decade.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We aim to deploy 60,000 charging points at public carparks and private premises by 2030 – more ambitious than our previous target of 28,000.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: To catalyse partnership between the public and private sectors, I will set aside $30 million over the next five years for EV-related initiatives, such as measures to improve charging provision at private premises.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: To further encourage the early adoption of electric cars, we will narrow the cost differential between electric cars and internal combustion engine cars, or ICE cars.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: I will lower the Additional Registration Fee floor to zero for electric cars, from January 2022 to December 2023.

sections.label: Petrol duty rate increases
sections.summary: Petrol duty rates will be raised by 15 cents per litre for premium petrol and 10 cents per litre for intermediate petrol.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: To build on the momentum, I will raise petrol duty rates: for premium petrol, the duty will be raised by 15 cents per litre; for intermediate petrol, the duty will be raised by 10 cents per litre.

sections.label: Offsets for petrol duty revenue
sections.summary: Most of the expected revenue increase from the petrol duty changes will be given out through offsets estimated to cost $113 million.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Most of the expected revenue increase from the petrol duty changes in the coming year will be given out through the offsets, estimated to cost $113 million.

sections.label: Rail network and green bonds
sections.summary: Within this decade, more than $60 billion will be spent to expand and renew the rail network, with the Government issuing green bonds on select public infrastructure projects.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Within this decade, we will be spending more than $60 billion to expand and renew our rail network.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The Government will take the lead by issuing green bonds on select public infrastructure projects.

sections.label: Government green bond issuance
sections.summary: Government green bonds will deepen market liquidity, attract green issuers, capital and investors, and anchor Singapore as a green finance hub, with up to $19 billion of public sector green projects identified.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The issuance of green bonds by the Government will build on these efforts by deepening market liquidity for green bonds, attracting green issuers, capital and investors, and anchoring Singapore as a green finance hub.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We have identified up to $19 billion of public sector green projects as a start.

sections.label: Carbon tax levels
sections.summary: Budget 2018 announced a carbon tax of $5 per tonne of greenhouse gas emissions from 2019 to 2023, rising to between $10 and $15 per tonne by 2030.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: In Budget 2018, we announced a carbon tax level of $5 per tonne of greenhouse gas emissions from 2019 to 2023, to be increased to between $10 and $15 per tonne by 2030.

sections.label: Review of carbon tax
sections.summary: Singapore will review the trajectory and level of the carbon tax post-2023 in consultation with industry and expert groups.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: As a responsible member of the international community, Singapore will be expected to do more, along with other countries, as climate change issues take on greater gravity.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We will therefore review the trajectory and level of the carbon tax, post-2023, in consultation with industry and expert groups.

sections.label: Carbon tax level review
sections.summary: An appropriate carbon tax level is a key lever, with the review outcome to be announced at Budget 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: An appropriate carbon tax level is one of the key levers to spur the reduction of our carbon footprint, promote industry innovation and green growth, while maintaining Singapore's overall economic competitiveness.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We will announce the outcome of the review at Budget 2022, to give time for businesses to adjust to any revision in the carbon tax trajectory.

sections.label: Enterprise Sustainability Programme launch
sections.summary: The Government will launch the Enterprise Sustainability Programme to help enterprises, especially SMEs, use resources efficiently and develop green products.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The Government will support our businesses to seize new opportunities in the green economy.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We will be launching the Enterprise Sustainability Programme.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: This will help enterprises, especially SMEs, use resources more efficiently and develop new green products and solutions.

sections.label: Past Reserves and COVID-19 package
sections.summary: Of $52 billion, $42.7 billion of Past Reserves is expected, with $11 billion committed for the FY2021 COVID-19 Resilience Package.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Of the $52 billion, we expect to utilise $42.7 billion of Past Reserves.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: For FY2021, we are committing $11 billion for the COVID-19 Resilience Package, to tackle the immediate and extraordinary challenges that COVID-19 continues to pose.

sections.label: Total expected draw on Past Reserves
sections.summary: The total expected draw on Past Reserves over FY2020 and FY2021 will be up to $53.7 billion.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Putting together the proposed draw of up to $11 billion in FY2021, and the $42.7 billion of Past Reserves that we now expect to draw in FY2020, the total expected draw on Past Reserves over FY2020 and FY2021 will be up to $53.7 billion.

sections.label: Healthcare spending increase
sections.summary: Before COVID-19, recurrent spending needs were expected to rise structurally, with healthcare spending tripling from $3.7 billion in FY2010 to $11.3 billion in FY2019.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Prior to COVID-19, we were already expecting a structural increase in our recurrent spending needs, especially in areas such as healthcare.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We have tripled our government spending on healthcare within a decade, from $3.7 billion in FY2010 to $11.3 billion in FY2019.

sections.label: Timing of increase
sections.summary: The increase cannot be put off too long and must be made sometime during 2022 to 2025, sooner rather than later, subject to the economic outlook.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: However, we will not be able to put off the increase for too long.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We will have to make the move sometime during 2022 to 2025, and sooner rather than later, subject to the economic outlook.

sections.label: GST absorption and Assurance Package
sections.summary: GST on publicly-subsidised education and healthcare stays fully absorbed, and $6 billion is set aside for an Assurance Package.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: GST on publicly-subsidised education and healthcare will continue to be fully absorbed.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: And to help cushion the impact when the GST rate is raised, we have set aside $6 billion for an Assurance Package.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: This will effectively delay the effect of the GST rate increase for the majority of Singaporean households by at least five years.

sections.label: GST on imported low-value goods
sections.summary: GST will be extended to imported low-value goods from 1 January 2023, following other jurisdictions.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Several jurisdictions, including Australia, New Zealand and the European Union, have implemented or announced plans to implement the equivalent of GST on such goods.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: I will hence extend GST to imported low-value goods with effect from 1 January 2023.

sections.label: Proposed SINGA bond issuance
sections.summary: The Government intends to issue new bonds under a proposed Significant Infrastructure Government Loan Act and will table a Bill this year.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Having studied this extensively, the Government intends to issue new bonds under a proposed Significant Infrastructure Government Loan Act, or SINGA for short.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The Government will table a Bill in Parliament later this year.

sections.label: SINGA bonds for infrastructure
sections.summary: Under the proposed SINGA legislation, the Government will issue bonds to finance major, long-term infrastructure.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: With the proposed SINGA legislation, the Government will now issue bonds for an additional purpose of financing major, long-term infrastructure.

sections.label: SINGA borrowing limit
sections.summary: A limit of $90 billion will be set for borrowing under SINGA as a safeguard.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: As a safeguard, we will set a limit of $90 billion for borrowing under SINGA.

sections.label: Past Reserves for economic investments
sections.summary: If conditions deteriorate, the Government will seek the President's consideration to use Past Reserves for economic investments.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Should the public health and economic situation deteriorate and the need arise, the Government will seek the President’s consideration for the use of Past Reserves to support these economic investments to ensure Singapore emerges stronger from this crisis.

sections.label: FY2020 Budget deficit
sections.summary: For FY2020, an overall Budget deficit of $64.9 billion, or 13.9% of GDP, is expected.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: For FY2020, we expect an overall Budget deficit of $64.9 billion, or 13.9% of GDP.

sections.label: Plans and overall deficit
sections.summary: Plans to emerge stronger are explained, with measures giving a fiscal boost and an expected overall deficit of $11.0 billion, or 2.2% of GDP.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: I have also explained our plans to emerge stronger by pressing on with economic and workforce transformation, strengthening our social compact and building a sustainable future for all.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: These measures will impart a considerable fiscal boost to the economy, and we expect an overall deficit of $11.0 billion, or 2.2% of GDP.

sections.label: COVID-19 Resilience Package
sections.summary: The Government will set aside $11 billion in this year's Budget for the COVID-19 Resilience Package to help people and stressed sectors.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The Government will set aside $11 billion in this year’s Budget for the COVID-19 Resilience Package to continue helping our people and the sectors which are still under stress.

sections.label: Business innovation and transformation
sections.summary: $24 billion will be set aside to encourage businesses to innovate, transform and seize regional and global market opportunities, creating good employment opportunities.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The COVID-19 has also accelerated ongoing structural changes and introduced new areas of cooperation and competition.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: I will set aside $24 billion to encourage businesses to innovate, transform and seize opportunities in the regional and global markets, to create good employment opportunities for our people.

sections.label: Household Support Package
sections.summary: The Government will strive towards a loving and inclusive society, and a $900 million Household Support Package will provide additional short-term relief.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The Government will continue to strive towards forging a loving and inclusive society to cater for the needs of various groups of people.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: I will introduce a $900 million Household Support Package to provide our people with additional short-term relief.

sections.label: Petrol duty rates raised
sections.summary: Petrol duty rates will be raised today to encourage less use of petrol vehicles, with rebates to alleviate the burden.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: To encourage people to use less of vehicles that use petrol, the petrol duty rates will be raised today, but the Government will give various rebates to alleviate the burden of the people.

sections.label: GST increase and infrastructure loan
sections.summary: The GST rate must be raised between 2022 and 2025, a Significant Infrastructure Government Loan Bill will be introduced, and Past Reserves will fund the Covid-19 Resilience Package.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: However, in order to meet our recurrent expenditures, the GST rate increase cannot be put off too long.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: It has to be increased during the period from 2022 to 2025 and it should be implemented sooner rather than later.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The Government will also introduce a Significant Infrastructure Government Loan Bill in Parliament this year, in order to facilitate financing for our major, long-term infrastructure projects.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: In this Budget year, we will once again draw on our Past Reserves, to fund the Covid-19 Resilience Package.

sections.label: Budget packages and plans
sections.summary: The passage lists the COVID-19 Resilience Package, Household Support Package, economic and workforce transformation investments, and the Singapore Green Plan 2030.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The COVID-19 Resilience Package to re-open safely and sustain the momentum of our recovery.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The Household Support Package for our families, with greater support for families who need more help.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Our investments in economic and workforce transformation to emerge stronger.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The Singapore Green Plan 2030 to enhance sustainability and do our part to deal with climate change.

sections.label: Founding generation values and reserves
sections.summary: The founding generation's values of prudence to save and prepare for the long-term built up reserves that provided strong support.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: In particular, the values of our founding generation – of prudence to save and prepare for the long-term – enabled us to build up our reserves, which provided us the strong support we needed.

sections.label: Interconnected world and pandemic fragmentation
sections.summary: The world is more deeply interconnected and interdependent than ever, but the pandemic has exposed and enlarged crack lines and fragmentation in many parts.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The world is more deeply interconnected and interdependent than ever.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: But this pandemic has exposed and enlarged crack lines and fragmentation in many parts.

sections.label: Parliament approves financial policy, debate adjourned
sections.summary: The Question seeks Parliament's approval of the Government's financial policy for 1 April 2021 to 31 March 2022, and the debate stands adjourned.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: The Question is, "That Parliament approves the financial policy of the Government for the financial year 1 April 2021 to 31 March 2022." In accordance with paragraph (1) of Standing Order No 89, the debate now stands adjourned.
